key_insight: E-prop trained a biologically inspired spiking controller to match backpropagation through time at 100% survival, while more biologically faithful schemes performed substantially worse.
engineering_relevance: Biologically inspired spiking networks show promise for humanoid locomotion control, but learning-rule choice strongly affects performance.
method: Distill a reinforcement-learning expert policy using dataset aggregation.
Compare a fixed recurrent reservoir, reward-modulated STDP, e-prop, and backpropagation through time.
Evaluate locomotion survival and demonstrate brief stepping on the full-size Unitree H1-2.
evidence_signal: Reported survival rates were 100% for e-prop and backpropagation through time, approximately 43.7% for the fixed reservoir, and approximately 11% for reward-modulated STDP.
watch_item: Brief hardware stepping does not establish sustained, robust real-world locomotion or transfer to living neural cultures.
paper_title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
